{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Clinical Development Funding Agreement (Execution Version)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer / PB side) 
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings, redlines and walk-away items

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Execution Version against the playbook and identified **seven deviations** out of eighteen rules tested; the remaining eleven rules are compliant, several on terms materially better than our preferred position.

The single **critical** issue is the absence of any aggregate monetary cap on liability: § 15.11 is the only limitation-of-liability provision, and while the indirect/consequential waiver is mutual, direct liability on both sides is unlimited. We have inserted a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims, drafted so as not to disturb the Article 6 / § 14.2 payment architecture.

The **high**-severity issue is assignment and change of control. § 14.2.6 gives SFJ a sole-discretion right to terminate the entire Agreement on a Change of Control of PB and to accelerate payment of 150% of Development Costs — squarely the walk-away case under that rule. § 15.6 compounds this: the consent-free Affiliate/successor proviso is mutual, consent carries no reasonableness standard, and there is no bar on assignment to a PB competitor.

The termination-economics package is the other area of real exposure. § 14.2.1 requires us to pay **300% of Development Costs** on SFJ's termination for our uncured material breach, expressed as being "in lieu of any claim for damages" (§ 14.4.2) — a punitive, breach-triggered liquidated amount payable by the Customer. Our nominal at-will exit at § 14.2.2 is illusory in playbook terms: it is unavailable until SFJ has funded USD 60m, lapses at first Regulatory Approval, and costs 300% of Development Costs to exercise, while SFJ's own exits at §§ 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 are exercisable at any time in its sole discretion. **Automated repair of the LD and T4C redlines did not verify and both require manual drafting before the turn goes out.**

Lower-severity but worth pressing: SFJ has no third-party IP infringement indemnity while our § 12.1.2(f) indemnity covers infringement by either Party's performance; SFJ owns the Trial Data Package outright under § 11.1.1.4 with no interim licence or use right reserved to us; and SFJ gives no performance warranty at all, with § 13.6.2 disclaiming everything outside Article 13.

On the credit side, exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitments, audit and auto-renewal exposure are all nil or run in our favour, and the post-termination transition regime in § 14.3 (data package assignment, Product Filings, trial hand-over at our election, CRO/Site/Vendor assignments) is materially better than our preferred position.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 15.11 (per § 15.3.2 ref); arbitration waiver at § 15.10.2.4 | No aggregate cap anywhere; mutual cap with uncapped Excluded Claims inserted (redline verified) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.2.6; § 15.6 (Term and Termination) | Walk-away: SFJ sole-discretion CoC termination + 150% acceleration; consent not reasonableness-qualified, no competitor bar (redline verified) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 3.19; § 2.4; § 3.14.1.1 / § 3.14.2.1 | No exclusivity on us; the only covenant runs against SFJ and benefits us |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | Article 11 (IP and PII) | Better than preferred: PB retains sole and exclusive ownership of Existing IP and Trial Inventions |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3.19; § 7.5 | No PB-side field-of-use or competing-product restraint; § 7.5 covenants are financing/collateral in nature |
| Medium | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 14.2.1; § 14.4.2 (Term and Termination) | 300% of Development Costs on our uncured breach, in lieu of damages — punitive. **Redline failed verification; manual drafting required** |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Article 9 (§§ 9.1–9.2); § 3.6; § 3.5.5; § 5.4.4.3 | No audit, inspection or system-access right over us; better than preferred |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | § 15.9; § 15.10 | Delaware law sits at the fallback; ICDR arbitration seated in New York under the FAA, IP carve-out, injunctive relief preserved |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7.4 (Security Interest) | No MFN mechanic; the "not less favorable" language is lien-priority protection only |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | §§ 4.1, 4.2, 4.2.3; Article 6 (§§ 6.1.1–6.1.2, 6.7) | No take-or-pay on us; payment flow runs toward us, Approval Payments contingent on Regulatory Approval |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (fallback) | § 15.16 | Mutual, solicitation-only, scoped to involved personnel, general-advertising carve-out; **tail duration redacted [***]** |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 14.1; § 14.2.2 | Single fixed Term; no auto-renewal, evergreen or notice window anywhere |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant | § 14.3 (§§ 14.3.1–14.3.5); § 10.3; § 11.1.1.4; § 14.4.3 | Above preferred: data/filings assigned to us, trial hand-over at our election, certified destruction; **periods redacted [***]** |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12.1.1; § 12.1.2(f); §§ 12.2.1–12.2.5 | No SFJ IP infringement limb while ours covers either Party's performance; fallback SFJ IP indemnity added with 3x super-cap (redline verified) |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 11.1.1.4; def. 1.1.193; §§ 6.1, 14.2–14.3 | SFJ owns the Trial Data Package with no interim licence to us; fallback perpetual royalty-free licence back added (redline verified) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 12.3.1–12.3.4 | Exceeds structural expectations (mutual, additional insured, certificates, A- rating); **limits redacted [***]**, no dedicated cyber line |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 14.2.2; §§ 14.2.6, 14.2.10 | Our exit gated at USD 60m funding, lapses at first Approval, costs 300%; SFJ exits at will. **Redline failed verification; manual drafting required** |
| Low | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 13.5; § 13.6.2 (Reps and Warranties) | No SFJ performance warranty and no remedy; fallback § 13.5.1 inserted (redline verified) |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **SFJ's change-of-control termination right (§ 14.2.6).** A sole-discretion right to terminate the entire Agreement on a Change of Control of PB, coupled with accelerated payment of 150% of Development Costs, is the express walk-away case under the assignment rule. Our redline converts this to a prohibition; we should not settle for a softened version of the right.
2. **Non-solicitation tail (§ 15.16) — contingent.** The tail is redacted ([***] after the Term). If the unredacted period exceeds 24 months, the clause moves into walk-away territory and must be revisited.
3. **Confirmed *not* triggered:** the governing law and venue walk-away test (§§ 15.9–15.10). The forum is ICDR arbitration seated in New York under the FAA, not mandatory arbitration seated abroad or in SFJ's home jurisdiction.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-draft the two failed redlines before the turn issues.** The LD edit to § 14.2.1 and the T4C edit to § 14.2.2 / §§ 14.2.6, 14.2.10 did not verify and need manual drafting. Positions: no liquidated damages or penalty payable by PB on SFJ's termination for breach (preserving the purchase and exclusive-remedy mechanics); unconditional PB convenience exit on 90 days' notice with the exit fee capped at three months' Development Costs; SFJ convenience termination effective only at end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice.
2. **Conform the parallel termination amounts.** If the § 14.2.1 change is accepted, conform §§ 14.2.5.2, 14.2.7 and 14.2.10. Note § 14.4.2's cap on SFJ's damages claim benefits us and is not to be reopened.
3. **Issue the four verified redlines** — mutual liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims (after § 15.11); assignment package (delete § 14.2.6 CoC right, narrow the § 15.6 free-assignment proviso to PB, add reasonableness standard, add competitor bar); SFJ third-party IP indemnity; Trial Data Package licence-back; and the § 13.5.1 performance warranty.
4. **Obtain unredacted figures in diligence:** insurance limits (§§ 12.3.1–12.3.4) against our preferred thresholds; the non-solicit tail (§ 15.16); the transition periods in §§ 14.3.3–14.3.4; and the further sum payable for the Trial Data Package under § 11.1.1.4.
5. **File notes for negotiation discipline.** (i) Resist any argument that "sufficient detail to verify compliance" in § 9.2 implies an access right; if SFJ seeks an express audit right, apply the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, SFJ's cost, no system access). (ii) The § 7.5.5 SFJ consent right over non-Excluded Licensing Transactions constrains our licensing freedom and is tracked as a separate commercial term, not under the non-compete rule. (iii) There is no express interim licence for us to use the Trial Data Package pre-closing; the licence-back redline addresses this.
6. **Preserve the favourable terms.** Do not reopen § 3.19 (SFJ exclusivity), Article 11 ownership provisions other than § 11.1.1.4, § 13.6.1, § 14.3, § 14.4.2 or the insurance regime — each runs in our favour."}
